extracted.intended_audience: scholars, editors, translators, and advanced students preparing editions or commentaries of Euclid's Elements
extracted.subtask_description: Scholarly notes and editorial guidance for producing a corrected, clarified, and pedagogically useful edition/translation of Euclid's Elements, including which demonstrations, definitions, words, and cases should be retained, corrected, or restored. Emphasizes fidelity to Greek/Arabic/Latin traditions and clarity for learners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include all cases that require different demonstrations
rubrics_metrics.description: “no case of a proposition that requires a different demonstration, ought to be omitted.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where separate cases require genuinely different proofs (not merely routine variants), each case must be given its own demonstration rather than omitted as 'easy'. Restore cases missing from some manuscripts (e.g., Greek omissions) using other traditions (Arabic/Latin) when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permit indirect (apagogic) demonstrations when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Some propositions cannot be demonstrated directly; indirect (apagogic) demonstrations are sometimes necessary and legitimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not excoriate indirect proofs wholesale: if no direct proof can be given from antecedent principles (example: Prop. I of Book III), an apagogic proof is appropriate and should be used and explained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer demonstrations that minimize extra dependencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose proofs that do not introduce unnecessary additional propositions as intermediate steps (avoid proofs which force use of extra lemmas not immediately implied).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple proofs exist, prefer the one that derives the result from the fewest and earliest propositions (example: avoid using prop. 26 b.1 when prop. 4 b.1 suffices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unnecessary division of a proposition into multiple cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not split a proposition into redundant cases when the same construction and demonstration serve all cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove useless repetitions introduced by later editors (e.g., some propositions divided into three cases where two or one suffice), and consolidate cases when appropriate (Campanus/Clavius noted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure constructions only require previously given methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructions in a proposition must not presuppose methods or operations (e.g., dividing lines into equal parts) that have not yet been proved or shown earlier in the Elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a construction uses a technique first proved later in the text, replace it with a construction that uses only already-established procedures (example: change a construction requiring division into equal parts before Book VI's Prop. 9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restore missing converses and complementary parts when justified
rubrics_metrics.description: If a converse or complementary part of a proposition is missing in a tradition, add it when it should logically accompany the original statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add missing converses (noting provenance), as in places where the converse was omitted but ought to have been included and demonstrated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use precise technical vocabulary and correct translations
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer exact geometric terms (e.g., distinguish meeting vs. touching; use 'tangit'/'touch' where appropriate; use 'circumference' rather than loose 'circle' when meant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correct mistranslations (e.g., replace 'contingit' with 'tangit' in specific definitions), follow the Greek compound verbs when they carry distinct meanings, and correct Latin/English renderings that alter sense (example: 'rursus inclinetur' should be 'rursus inflectatur').

rubrics_metrics.name: Place definitions and conceptually related material in their proper order
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions (and the placement of special definitions like 'compound ratio' or 'compound proportion') should appear where they are logically needed and historically intended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Move or restore definitions to their proper locations (example: place the definition of compound ratio between defs XI and XII of Book V rather than leaving Theon's misplaced version in Book VI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amend or insert words necessary for correctness; remove spurious words
rubrics_metrics.description: Add missing words required for logical truth or remove superfluous/erroneous insertions by later editors (e.g., add 'continual' before 'proportionals'; add/remove 'any whatever' where appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the Greek lacks necessary words or contains extra words introduced by an editor, correct the text to preserve mathematical correctness and logical consistency, and annotate such emendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not substitute corollaries for legitimate missing demonstrations
rubrics_metrics.description: A corollary should not be used to cover for a missing primary demonstration; the original legitimate demonstration must be sought or restored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a corollary has been unskilfully annexed and replaced a demonstration that belongs elsewhere, restore the legitimate demonstration and reposition the corollary appropriately (example: Cor. IV prop. B. V.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer clearer/simpler demonstrations when the original is cumbersome
rubrics_metrics.description: When the original Greek or later Latin demonstration is awkward, a clearer equivalent demonstration (even if different) is preferable if it conveys the true meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt simpler methods (as with Clairault's or Simpson's alternatives) provided they are faithful to the proposition and avoid introducing unsound dependencies; note the change and justify it in commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-check multiple manuscript/traditional sources and integrate corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult Greek, Arabic, and Latin traditions (e.g., Commandine, Theon, Clavius, Arabic translations) to identify omissions, corruptions, and better constructions and to restore Euclid's likely original intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where traditions differ, prefer readings that preserve logical structure and earlier dependency order; explicitly mention provenance of restorations and differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: When definitions are metaphysical or pedagogical, clarify their role for learners
rubrics_metrics.description: Some definitions (e.g., the third definition of ratio) are metaphysical/summary and not strictly mathematical; these should be explained or set apart for beginners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explanatory commentary (as Barrow does) indicating that certain definitions are for intuition rather than deduction and emphasize the 'accurate mathematical definitions' that follow; annotate which definitions can be omitted without loss to rigorous development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure referenced propositions actually imply the stated conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not rely on a referenced proposition that does not directly yield the asserted consequence (avoid circular or misleading references).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that every invoked prior proposition legitimately supplies the needed result (example: avoid invoking prop. 26 b.1 where it does not immediately give the equality claimed). If not, replace reference with the correct antecedent or rework the proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restore omitted demonstrations or cases removed by careless editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Detect cases where editors (Theon, other hands) have omitted parts of demonstrations or entire cases and restore them when they are essential to completeness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use alternate traditions (Arabic, Latin) and internal logical requirements to reconstruct omitted steps; annotate such restorations and the reasoning behind them (examples throughout Books II–V notes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unskilful interpolations that change meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not retain phrases or clauses evidently inserted by ignorant editors that alter logical flow or introduce nonsense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where corrupt passages are detected (e.g., gratuitous words inserted in Greek), correct the text and justify the emendation; prefer readings consistent with mathematical sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate geometric facts directly where feasible
rubrics_metrics.description: When a geometric fact (e.g., circle touches a straight line) can be shown directly, prefer direct demonstrations unless an indirect route is shorter and fully justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For uniformity and pedagogy, choose direct demonstrations in a book's propositions when they are shorter and clearer (the editor chose direct methods in Book IV where shorter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotate editorial choices and provenance of alternative proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: When adopting non-original proofs or moving definitions, explicitly note the source (e.g., Clairault, Simpson, Commandine, Barrow) and the reason for the editorial choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide readers with historical and logical justification for changes (so they can evaluate fidelity vs clarity), including when a translator/editor follows Arabic or Latin variants rather than the Greek.
